articles.title: KI bei der Geldanlage: Wie sicher sind ChatGPT-Anlagetipps?
articles.preview: KI wird zunehmend für Anlageberatung eingesetzt. Experten warnen jedoch vor Risiken und Fehlern bei den KI-basierten Empfehlungen.

summary.t: Die Nutzung von KI-Modellen wie ChatGPT und Claude für Anlageentscheidungen nimmt zu. Eine Umfrage zeigt, dass bereits jeder vierte Mensch in Deutschland sich an diese Systeme wendet, um Rat zu erhalten. Studien deuten auf ein Potenzial hin, aber auch auf mögliche Fehlerquellen.

Wissenschaftliche Untersuchungen haben gezeigt, dass KI-Modelle in der Lage sind, die Wertentwicklung von Portfolios mit professionell verwalteten Portfolios zu vergleichen. Forscher der Stanford University kommen zu dem Ergebnis, dass KI brauchbare Finanztipps liefern kann.

Es besteht jedoch Vorsicht geboten. KI-Modelle können Informationen erfinden oder falsche Zusammenhänge darstellen. Die europäische Wertpapieraufsicht ESMA warnt vor einer alleinigen Nutzung von Chatbots. Zudem können die Antworten der KI von Werbeanzeigen beeinflusst werden.

Die Entwicklung von KI im Finanzbereich könnte den Zugang zum Kapitalmarkt für Menschen erleichtern. Experten sehen die Möglichkeit, dass KI als Orientierungshilfe und für die Simulation von Anlageszenarien genutzt werden kann.

articles.title: The big questions remaining after Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO prospectus
articles.preview: Anthropic, a leading AI lab, recently filed an extensive S-1 prospectus revealing key details about its operations and financial projections. The filing highlights significant revenue growth and substantial financial resources, but also raises questions about future growth rates and valuation expectations.

summary.t: Anthropic reported $16.29 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026, a significant increase from the $1.16 billion recorded in the first half of 2025. Revenue growth slowed to approximately 47% in the third quarter following a 144% increase in the second quarter. The company’s cost of revenue is $2.38 billion, resulting in an implied gross margin of 85%. Analysts are questioning how quickly revenue can grow to meet expectations and the cost associated with generating each additional dollar.

A substantial portion of Anthropic’s cost of revenue, approximately $2.38 billion, is attributed to compute and infrastructure costs. The company has previously struggled to secure sufficient compute capacity from cloud providers, operating in a ‘compute-constrained environment.’ Questions remain about whether compute costs will continue to fall faster than demand increases, and whether Anthropic can secure enough capacity to meet customer needs.

Seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, hold significant voting power through a single Class F share, granting them 50.1% of total voting power. Anthropic’s unique capital and corporate governance structure, with no direct precedent, raises questions about investor acceptance and potential impact on the share price. The company plans to issue additional class shares, but the details of this plan are currently unknown.

articles.title: 500 Milliarden Dollar vernichtet: Google-Bilanz verursacht historischen Kurssturz
articles.preview: Google hat heute einen historischen Kurssturz erlebt, der rund 500 Milliarden Dollar an Marktwert vernichtet hat. Dies ist hauptsächlich auf Bedenken hinsichtlich der Rentabilität von KI-Investitionen und unerfüllten Umsatz-Erwartungen zurückzuführen.

summary.t: Der Aktienkurs von Alphabet, dem Mutterkonzern von Google, ist heute um 13 Prozent eingebrochen. Dieser Absturz führte zu einem Verlust von rund 500 Milliarden US-Dollar an Marktwert innerhalb eines Tages. Dieser Kursverlust ist einer der größten in der Börsenhistorie. Der Absturz belastete den US-Aktienmarkt, insbesondere die Technologiebörse Nasdaq, die um 1,4 Prozent nachgab.

Die Sorge, dass KI-Investitionen nicht rentabel sind, sowie die Tatsache, dass Google die Umsatz-Erwartungen der Anleger im vergangenen Quartal nicht erfüllte, trugen zu dem Kursverlust bei. Die Furcht, dass alte Geschäftsmodelle wegfallen, betrifft die gesamte Technologiebranche.

Die Google Services Sparte, die Suchwerbung und YouTube umfasst, erwirtschaftete 96,3 Milliarden Dollar, was unter den Erwartungen der Analysten von 98,5 Milliarden Dollar lag. Zudem gab das Unternehmen mehr Geld aus, als es einnahm, was auf hohe Betriebskosten und einen negativen freien Cashflow hindeutet.

Die KI verändert die Art und Weise, wie Nutzer nach Informationen suchen. Die Google-Suche wuchs zwar um 12 Prozent, aber die KI-gestützte Suche kann den Bedarf an traditionellen Links reduzieren. Google versucht, das Suchgeschäft um KI herum umzugestalten, während konkurrierende Unternehmen ebenfalls in KI-Chatbots investieren.

articles.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
articles.preview: OpenAI will now respect signals from robots.txt to manage AI training data. This allows website operators to directly state their preferences to OpenAI.

articles.title: Community safety report and new protections for teens
articles.preview: OpenAI is implementing enhanced safety measures within ChatGPT, focusing on violence prevention. The company is also establishing a public safety reporting system.

articles.title: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
articles.preview: Microsoft is planning to borrow $25 billion through the issuance of bonds. This financing will be used to support the company's significant investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

summary.t: Microsoft announced it will issue $25 billion in bonds. The company’s AAA credit rating allows it to access favorable financing terms. The bond offering is expected to close on November 4th.

articles.title: Fair use benefits everyone
articles.preview: OpenAI is releasing documents detailing how fair use supports AI training. These materials come from a diverse group of experts, including creators and legal professionals.

articles.title: Schwarzer Tag für Alphabet : US-Anleger verlieren den KI-Optimismus
articles.preview: Alphabet hat einen dramatischen Kursverlust von 13 Prozent erlebt. Dies hat zu erheblichen Verlusten an der Wall Street geführt.

summary.t: Die Aktie von Alphabet, dem Mutterkonzern von Google, stürzte um fast 13 Prozent ab. Der Börsenwert schrumpfte um rund 460 Milliarden Dollar, was den größten Marktkapitalisierungsverlust eines einzelnen Unternehmens an einem Tag in der Geschichte darstellt. Der Umsatz enttäuschte, und der Konzern ging operativ in die roten Zahlen.

Die Abwärtsbewegung von Alphabet führte zu einem Rückgang der wichtigsten US-Indizes. Der Dow-Jones Index verlor 0,2 Prozent, der S&P 500 sank um 0,3 Prozent und der Nasdaq verzeichnete einen Rückgang von 1,4 Prozent.
Auch Aktien von Microsoft sanken um 0,2 Prozent, obwohl der Konzern einen hohen Mittelzufluss von 18,6 Milliarden Dollar erwirtschaftete.

articles.title: Alphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of search
articles.preview: Alphabet’s latest earnings report revealed a significant revenue miss, primarily driven by a slowdown in search growth. Simultaneously, Google is heavily investing in AI infrastructure and services, particularly through its Gemini model.

summary.t: Alphabet’s search and other segment revenue grew by 12% to approximately $63 billion, falling short of estimates for the second consecutive quarter. Despite a five-year high in search query growth, the gap between usage and revenue is widening due to increased use of AI-powered bots. The search segment’s growth rate decreased from 19% to 17% to 12% over the last three quarters.

Alphabet is investing heavily in AI infrastructure and services, particularly through its Gemini model, to compete with companies like OpenAI. The company’s cloud business saw a more than doubling of revenue to nearly $31 billion, and a backlog of $560 billion. Google is deploying Gemini across its ads infrastructure and adding new AI capabilities to product listing ads. Advertisers are rapidly adopting Gemini tools, generating over 1.5 billion campaign assets in the third quarter.

The earnings report resulted in a record-breaking $13% stock drop and a negative free cash flow of $9 billion for the quarter. Google’s cloud division is experiencing significant growth, with revenue increasing by 48% to $33.2 billion. The company’s cloud backlog reached approximately $560 billion.

articles.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
articles.preview: OpenAI has released an updated Model Spec. This document focuses on creating AI with improved capabilities and benefits.

articles.title: AI buildout hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts
articles.preview: Google and Microsoft have lowered their forecasts for capital expenditures related to artificial intelligence infrastructure. This shift suggests a potential slowdown in the rapid expansion of AI development.

summary.t: Microsoft reduced its annual capital expenditure forecast to $170 billion, initially projected at $175 billion. Alphabet maintained its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion, both figures falling short of previous expectations. These adjustments signal a potential cooling of investment in AI infrastructure.

Significant delays in the availability of graphics processing units (GPUs) from third-party providers are impacting Microsoft’s plans. CFO Amy Hood indicated these delays won’t resolve until the first half of 2027, highlighting a critical bottleneck in the AI buildout.

Several neocloud companies, including CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN, saw their stock prices decline following the announcements. Oracle, a major AI infrastructure investor, also experienced a drop. These neoclouds rely heavily on external capital and currently lack investment-grade credit ratings.

articles.title: As AI becomes more fractured, one name stands out: AMD
articles.preview: The artificial intelligence sector is experiencing instability, with several companies facing significant declines. AMD is currently the most promising investment based on specific criteria, despite broader market concerns.

summary.t: Several AI-focused companies, including CoreWeave (-15.5%) and IREN (-20%), have experienced sharp declines. This instability is fueled by concerns surrounding data center spending and is impacting chipmakers, particularly those supplying AMD.
AMD’s stock price dropped 8.1% due to Meta’s financing plans and a supply warning from Lam Research. Consensus estimates predict nearly 62% YoY revenue growth and 41% YoY EPS growth for AMD in Q3.

The author's investment screen prioritizes companies with strong growth, including revenue and EPS growth rates exceeding 5% and 7% respectively, alongside positive ROE and ROIC metrics. Currently, AMD is the only company meeting these stringent criteria.
AMD CEO Lisa Su stated plans to substantially increase supply in 2027, reflecting the ongoing demand from AI orders. This highlights the significant capacity constraints within the sector.

articles.title: Alphabet drags on Nasdaq futures as the stock faces a record post-earnings loss
articles.preview: Alphabet shares are plummeting in premarket trading due to disappointing earnings, and Microsoft’s strong results and reduced spending are impacting cloud stocks. The market is bracing for a volatile day ahead with Amazon’s earnings release.

summary.t: Alphabet’s stock fell over 10% in premarket trading. This marks the first time since Q4 2022 that the company missed both earnings per share (EPS) and revenue targets. Concerns are centered around Google’s Search, with investors worried about AI chat and agents impacting search volumes.

Microsoft shares rose in premarket trading, driven by strong growth in Azure, which increased by 48%. The company also provided a revenue forecast of up to $97 billion for the second quarter. Microsoft’s capital expenditure (capex) guidance was lowered to $170 billion for the full year.

articles.title: Meta outlook revised downward by S&P on cash flow and capex concerns
articles.preview: S&P Global Ratings has lowered Meta's outlook due to concerns about its cash flow and significant investments in artificial intelligence. This downgrade reflects uncertainty surrounding Meta's financial performance and its ability to generate profits from new AI ventures.

summary.t: S&P Global Ratings downgraded Meta’s credit rating from AA- stable to AA- negative. This move places Meta’s debt within the ‘junk bond’ category, which is below S&P’s highest rating of AAA.
The downgrade stems from Meta’s projected high capital expenditures, estimated between $135 billion and $145 billion for the year.

articles.title: Cramer’s week ahead: Expect more volatility as tech earnings, midterms loom
articles.preview: Jim Cramer predicts continued market volatility due to upcoming events and earnings reports. He advises investors to focus on high-quality companies despite recent market turbulence.

summary.t: The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.3% through Wednesday before plummeting 2.9% Friday, resulting in a total weekly decline of 2%. Similarly, the S&P 500 gained 1.6% through Wednesday, followed by a 1.8% drop Friday, ending the week with a 0.6% decrease. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also reversed course, rising 0.5% through Wednesday before falling 1.1% Friday, finishing down 0.9% for the week.

Several major companies are reporting earnings this week, including Apple, Palantir, Advanced Micro Devices, Pfizer, Amgen, CVS Health, McDonald’s, and Kimberly-Clark. Cramer anticipates positive results from Palantir and AMD, while expressing concerns about CVS’s pharmacy benefit management business. He believes Kimberly-Clark will benefit from its merger with Kenvue.
The midterm elections are a significant factor, with potential shifts in congressional control raising concerns about data center projects.

articles.title: Nasdaq mit Rekordtagesverlust : Wall Street geht gefleddert ins Wochenende
articles.preview: Die Wall Street erlebte am Freitag einen historischen Einbruch. Besonders der Nasdaq verzeichnete den größten prozentualen Verlust seit Juni.

summary.t: Der Nasdaq verzeichnete einen prozentualen Tagesverlust von 2,9 Prozent und erreichte 25.437 Punkte. Der S&P 500 sank um 1,8 Prozent auf 7580 Punkte, während der Dow-Jones Index um 1,1 Prozent auf 51.770 Punkte fiel. Die Verkäufersignale resultierten aus den Quartalsergebnissen von Amazon und Intel.

Intel erlebte einen dramatischen Kursverfall von fast 30 Prozent. Der Chipkonzern warnte vor erheblichen Umsatzeinbußen aufgrund einer Fabrikkatastrophe in Israel und prognostizierte einen negativen Barmittelzufluss.

articles.title: Intel stock has worst day since 1970s, wiping about $12 billion off government's stake
articles.preview: Intel stock experienced a dramatic decline, marking its worst day since the 1970s. This downturn significantly impacted the U.S. government's investment in the company.

summary.t: Intel shares fell by 29% on Friday, representing their most significant decline since the 1970s. This drop was triggered by weaker-than-expected guidance, stemming from a plant shutdown in Israel and ongoing weakness in the PC market. The company's CEO, Lip-Bu Tan, is facing challenges in revitalizing Intel after missing the AI boom.

The U.S. government’s 10% stake in Intel lost approximately $12 billion on Friday. Nvidia also saw its stock value decrease by roughly $6 billion. This represents a substantial financial hit for the Trump administration.
Analysts downgraded Intel stock to neutral, citing significant weakness in the PC market and a high multiple for the stock.

articles.title: Marktbericht: Schwaches Ende einer starken Börsenwoche
articles.preview: Der DAX schließt die Woche mit einem Verlust ab. Schwache Zahlen aus dem Technologiesektor und steigende Ölpreise sind die Hauptursachen für den Rückgang.

summary.t: Der DAX schloss am Wochenschluss bei 25.818 Punkten, was einem Tagesverlust von 0,85 Prozent entspricht. Zuvor hatte der Index vier Tage in Folge gestiegen. Der MDAX verzeichnete ebenfalls einen Rückgang von 1,06 Prozent.

Der hohe Ölpreis, insbesondere durch Sorgen um einen möglichen Militärschlag zwischen den USA und dem Iran, sowie schwache Vorgaben aus dem US-Technologiereich trugen zum Rückgang bei. Die Entscheidung der EZB zur Stabilisierung der Zinsen unterstützte die Märkte jedoch zuvor.

Der MDAX schloss bei 30.472 Zählern. Die Ölpreise erreichten aufgrund der geopolitischen Unsicherheiten ihren höchsten Stand seit April. Der Rückgang der Verbraucherpreise in Deutschland auf 2,8 Prozent wurde durch Tankrabatte beeinflusst.
Intel-Aktien brachen an der Nasdaq um über 28 Prozent ein, was auf kritische Blicke auf die hohen Investitionen in KI-Technologie zurückzuführen ist.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Tech-Angst stoppt Dax-Rally
articles.preview: Der DAX konnte die Marke von 26.000 Punkten nicht halten und verzeichnete einen deutlichen Rückgang. Tech-Angst, insbesondere durch US-Tech-Unternehmen, führte zu einer starken Abwärtsbewegung im Leitindex.

summary.t: Der DAX schloss den Handel mit 25.818 Punkten, was einem Rückgang von 0,8 Prozent entspricht. Nach anfänglicher Konsolidierung dominierten die Belastungsfaktoren, vor allem im Technologiesektor.
Ein erneuter Ausverkauf bei US-Tech-Giganten wie Alphabet, Meta, Amazon und Intel verstärkte die Ängste. Die Intel-Aktie fiel um knapp 30 Prozent, während Amazon um 1,9 Prozent verlor.
Auch deutsche Unternehmen mit geringer KI-Beteiligung, wie Siemens Energy und Infineon, sanken deutlich.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Tech-Crash an der Wall Street - Intel schmiert fast 30 Prozent ab
articles.preview: An der Wall Street gab es heute einen deutlichen Crash im Technologiebereich. Besonders Intel verlor an Wert, während auch andere Aktien darunter litten.

summary.t: Der Dow-Jones-Index verzeichnete am Ende der Woche einen Rückgang von 0,3 Prozent und schloss bei 52.175 Punkten. Der S&P 500 verlor 1,2 Prozent an Wert. Diese Entwicklung deutet auf negative Stimmung am Markt hin.

articles.title: Musk and Zuckerberg echo Trump's push to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence' on earnings calls. Others do not
articles.preview: Following President Trump's directive, Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg have adopted the term "super intelligence" alongside other tech leaders. However, many tech CEOs remain resistant to fully embracing this rebranding effort.

summary.t: On September 29th, President Trump ordered the use of "super intelligence" within executive branch departments, aiming to promote AI growth in the U.S. with limited regulations. He subsequently announced a ban on the terms "AI" and "artificial intelligence" across all relevant documents via Truth Social. This initiative followed his hosting of an AI luncheon at the White House.

Musk and Zuckerberg, key Trump allies, aligned with this shift, rebranding SpaceX’s AI division to SpaceXSI and emphasizing Meta’s goal of delivering "personal superintelligence." Despite this, many tech giants, including Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet, continued to use the established "AI" terminology during their earnings calls. Notably, Amazon's Andy Jassy used the abbreviation over a dozen times, while Microsoft's Satya Nadella focused on "designing AI to empower people".

The push for "super intelligence" is already manifesting in corporate documents. Microsoft’s annual report included eight mentions of the term, and IBM CEO Arvind Krishna utilized "SI" alongside "AI" during his earnings call. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan attributed the chip industry’s demand to "super intelligence." Several tech leaders, including Nikesh Arora and Jensen Huang, publicly supported the initiative on social media.

articles.title: Marktbericht: Zweifel am KI-Boom wachsen
articles.preview: Zweifel am KI-Boom wachsen. Tech-Konzerne investieren stark in künstliche Intelligenz, doch die Einnahmen halten nicht Schritt.

summary.t: Anleger zeigen Skepsis gegenüber KI-Investitionen. Die Technologiebörse Nasdaq verzeichnete aufgrund der negativen Quartalsergebnisse von Amazon und Intel einen Kursrückgang. Die Börse akzeptiert Investitionen in KI und die dazugehörige Infrastruktur nicht mehr unkritisch, insbesondere wenn Schulden dafür aufgenommen werden müssen.

Die Aktie von Intel verlor nach dem Bericht zum dritten Quartal über ein Fünftel an Wert. Der Ausfall des Werks in Israel wird den Konzerngewinn um rund 300 Millionen Dollar reduzieren. Die Nachfrage nach Server-Prozessoren ist weiterhin hoch.
Amazons hohe Investitionen in KI-Rechenzentren belasten die Bilanz. Der Barmittelabfluss erhöhte sich auf 42,4 Milliarden Dollar. Amazon plant, die Investitionen im kommenden Jahr weiter zu steigern.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Ausverkauf wegen KI-Sorgen: Intel stürzen 25 Prozent ab
articles.preview: Der heutige Tag an der Börse war von starkem Rückgang geprägt, insbesondere im Technologiebereich. Die Sorgen um die Zukunft der Künstlichen Intelligenz haben zu erheblichen Kursverlusten geführt.

summary.t: Der S&P 500 Future verzeichnete einen Rückgang von 1,1 Prozent, während der Nasdaq-Future um 2,4 Prozent an Wert verlor. Diese Verluste spiegeln die allgemeine Unsicherheit wider, die durch die aktuellen Entwicklungen im Technologiebereich herrurscht.
Der Chip-Konzern Intel erlebte einen dramatischen Einbruch von 25 Prozent vorbörslich, aufgrund geringerer Gewinne und eines trüben Ausblicks.

articles.title: Tech scare trade hits Nasdaq futures while crypto reels from its biggest-ever hack
articles.preview: Tech stocks are plummeting, driven by disappointing earnings, while a massive cryptocurrency hack is sending shockwaves through the market. The Nasdaq futures are experiencing significant declines as a result of these combined events.

summary.t: Several major tech companies experienced substantial premarket losses. Intel’s shares dropped over 25% following weaker fourth-quarter guidance, reflecting concerns about the PC market. Amazon’s shares fell by over 7%, and Reddit experienced a 20% decline after the CEO’s warning about potential visitor drops. Alphabet shares remained flat after a 12% decrease on Thursday.

Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, reported a security incident resulting in $6.3 billion in assets being compromised. The exchange froze $3 billion, Circle froze $800 million, and Tether froze $1.56 billion related to the hack.

articles.title: Intel stock plunges 21% as chipmaker blames PC slowdown for weak guidance
articles.preview: Intel’s stock price has plummeted by over 20% following a weak earnings report. The company attributes this decline to a slowdown in the PC market and a significant disruption caused by a factory explosion.

summary.t: Intel reported a 21% revenue increase to $13.7 billion compared to the previous year’s $10.8 billion. However, the client computing and physical AI group experienced a 5% decrease to $8.1 billion, falling short of analyst estimates. Despite a 78% jump in data center and AI revenue to $7.3 billion, overall performance was negatively impacted.

Global PC shipments declined by 4% in the second quarter due to rising component costs. Intel’s CEO anticipates this slowdown will continue through the first half of next year. The company’s forecast reflects the impact of a $600 million revenue loss stemming from a factory explosion in Israel.

An explosion at an Intel fab in Israel, occurring earlier this month, resulted in two fatalities and serious injuries. This incident led to an ‘extended shutdown’ of the plant, impacting shipments of 10-nanometer chips. The company estimates a $600 million revenue loss over two quarters.

articles.title: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
articles.preview: Reddit shares plummeted following weak sales forecasts and plans to require all users to create official accounts. This shift comes amid a significant decline in search traffic from Google due to AI developments.

summary.t: Despite reporting a third-quarter earnings beat, with sales up 53% year-over-year and average revenue per user (ARPU) rising to $6.87, Reddit’s fourth-quarter sales guidance fell short of expectations, projecting a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion. This downward revision contributed to a 15% drop in the company’s share price.

A key factor driving Reddit’s concerns is the substantial decrease in search referral traffic from Google. CEO Steve Huffman stated that this traffic has declined “meaningfully” this quarter, primarily due to Google’s increased focus on AI-powered overviews. This shift, spurred by AI mode, is impacting the traditional flow of users to Reddit.

Reddit plans to implement a requirement for all users to create official accounts to access the platform. This represents a major change, marking the first time the site has moved away from its traditionally open access model. The company intends to begin testing this requirement in the fourth quarter, starting outside of the U.S.

Reddit is prioritizing growth among its app users and logged-in users, recognizing that these groups are more valuable to advertisers. Daily active uniques (DAUq) rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million, although U.S.

articles.title: Sorge ums Weihnachtsgeschäft: KI-Kosten reißen Milliardenloch in Amazons Bilanz
articles.preview: Amazon kämpft mit enormen Kosten für den Ausbau seiner KI-Infrastruktur, was zu einem erheblichen Einbruch der Gewinne führt. Die Investitionen belasten den Cashflow massiv und sorgen für Verunsicherung bei den Anlegern.

summary.t: Amazon meldete einen Barmittelabfluss von 42,4 Milliarden Dollar in den letzten drei Monaten – das entspricht einem Anstieg von nahezu 600 Prozent im Vergleich zum Vorjahr. Portfoliomanager Dave Wagner bezeichnete diese Entwicklung als besorgniserregend, da das operative Geschäft zwar profitabel ist, die Investitionen diesen Gewinn vollständig verschlingen. Die Situation ähnelt der von Google und Meta, die ebenfalls mit negativen Free Cash Flows zu kämpfen haben.

Der Konzern plant, im laufenden Jahr 220 Milliarden Dollar in den Ausbau seiner KI-Infrastruktur zu investieren. Google plant Investitionen von bis zu 205 Milliarden Dollar und Meta zwischen 135 und 145 Milliarden Dollar.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says Wall Street is punishing the wrong tech stocks
articles.preview: Jim Cramer believes Wall Street is overreacting to disappointing earnings, particularly within the tech sector. He argues investors are incorrectly selling stocks based on the performance of peer companies.

summary.t: On Thursday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average decreased by 0.4%, the S&P 500 also fell by 0.4%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped by 1.4%. This marked the end of a three-day winning streak for the market.

Jim Cramer highlighted cybersecurity stocks, specifically Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, and CrowdStrike. He argued that Fortinet's weak results were not indicative of a broader industry downturn, pointing to differences in their business models – Fortinet is hardware-focused, while the others offer broader security suites.
Similar concerns were raised regarding the enterprise software sector.

articles.title: Amazon posts negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion, holds 2026 capex unchanged
articles.preview: Amazon reported a significant negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion in the third quarter, driven by heavy AI investments. Despite this, the company remains committed to a $220 billion capital expenditure plan for 2026.

summary.t: Amazon experienced a substantial negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the trailing twelve months, a dramatic 386% increase year-over-year. This outflow was primarily due to increased spending on property and equipment related to AI investments. Previous negative free cash flow was $7.6 billion in the prior quarter.

Despite the negative cash flow, Amazon plans to maintain its capital expenditure forecast at $220 billion for 2026. Capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion during the third quarter, significantly higher than the estimated $58.7 billion.

Amazon’s cloud segment, AWS, showed strong growth, with sales soaring 39% year-over-year to $45.98 billion. Executives anticipate revenue growth rates of ‘over 40%’ for AWS in the coming years, citing investment in functionality and infrastructure.

articles.title: Amazon AWS posts 39% revenue growth as cloud rivals also accelerate
articles.preview: Amazon's AWS experienced a significant surge in revenue, exceeding expectations and driving growth in the cloud computing market. Major competitors like Alphabet and Microsoft are also accelerating their cloud expansion efforts, fueled by increasing demand for artificial intelligence.

summary.t: Amazon Web Services (AWS) reported revenue of $45.98 billion, representing a 39% increase year-over-year. This surpassed analyst estimates of $45.29 billion. The growth rate is the highest since the fourth quarter of 2021.
Alphabet’s Google Cloud business more than doubled in the third quarter, mirroring the accelerated growth seen across the major cloud providers.
